claims.claim: Expectancy-, context-, and learning-related placebo/nocebo mechanisms can produce measurable subjective responses and, in some paradigms, physiological changes.
claims.correction: Say “can produce measurable symptom reports and, under specific experimental conditions, physiological changes”; do not imply a uniform effect across diseases or that expectation alone reliably changes physiology.

citations.author: Albring et al.
citations.finding: In healthy volunteers, conditioned re-exposure was associated with reduced IL-2 production; mere verbal expectation of immunosuppression was not sufficient.

citations.author: Johansen, Brox, and Flaten
citations.finding: Saline plus analgesic expectation reduced pain ratings; negative expectation was associated with a larger cortisol increase. Pain relief was not correlated with cortisol or beta-endorphin.

claims.claim: Open-label placebo has been studied as an add-on to treatment as usual for chronic low back pain.
claims.correction: Use “studied in a randomized trial,” not “treats chronic low back pain.”

citations.author: Carvalho et al.
citations.finding: Randomized 83 analyzed participants with chronic low back pain to open-label placebo plus treatment as usual or treatment as usual alone for three weeks.

claims.claim: The Carvalho chronic-low-back-pain trial found improved self-reported pain and disability with open-label placebo plus usual care.
claims.correction: Say “the small, short trial reported greater self-reported pain and disability reductions than usual care alone.”

citations.author: Carvalho et al.
citations.finding: At three weeks, OLP+usual care had greater composite pain and Roland-Morris disability reductions than usual care (both P<.001); usual and maximum pain fell about 30% versus 9% and 16%, and disability fell 29% versus 0.02%.

claims.claim: Open-label placebo effects can occur without deception, and conscious belief that a pill contains active medicine is not the only possible route to an effect.
claims.correction: Do not say “belief is irrelevant.” Say “deception is not necessary in some studies; rationale credibility, conditioning, engagement, and expectation may still matter.”

citations.author: Carvalho et al.
citations.finding: Participants were explicitly told the pills were placebo; outcomes favored OLP+usual care over usual care alone.

citations.author: Albring et al.
citations.finding: Conditioned physiological effects occurred, while verbal expectation alone did not produce the measured immune effect.

claims.claim: Copables is a company offering physical placebo-containing protocols to consumers.
claims.correction: Say “Copables’ website depicts OLP gummies and says its 14-day protocols use placebos plus cognitive restructuring”; do not state pill ingredients are inert until ingredient/product records are checked.

citations.author: Copables Ltd.
citations.finding: The company site describes 14-day protocols using “placebos and cognitive restructuring,” depicts OLP gummies, and identifies the offering as a self-guided wellness program.

claims.claim: A phone-delivered intervention could reproduce some components of a physical placebo ritual.
claims.correction: Frame as a design hypothesis: “an app could deliver prompts, explanations, repetition, and engagement, but equivalence to a physical open-label placebo has not been demonstrated.”

citations.author: Lutz et al.
citations.finding: Review of digital-therapeutic trials found only 68 of 313 comparative studies used a digital sham, and none of those shams had been validated as a placebo comparator.

claims.claim: Ted Kaptchuk is associated with the Program in Placebo Studies & Therapeutic Encounter, Harvard Medical School, and Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center.
claims.correction: Use the current institutional wording: “Professor Emeritus at Harvard Medical School and research faculty at BIDMC.”

citations.author: Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center
citations.finding: Current profile identifies Kaptchuk as Professor Emeritus at Harvard Medical School, a BIDMC research-faculty member, and links the Program in Placebo Studies & Therapeutic Encounter.

strongest_evidence.author: Carvalho et al.
strongest_evidence.finding: Primary randomized evidence for the chronic-low-back-pain claim; measures were self-reported pain and disability over three weeks.

strongest_evidence.author: Albring et al.
strongest_evidence.finding: Primary evidence that learned placebo-related mechanisms can affect a measured immune marker, while also limiting an expectation-only interpretation.

strongest_evidence.author: Lutz et al.
strongest_evidence.finding: Systematic review establishing that digital-sham methodology exists but is heterogeneous and inadequately validated.

counterevidence.author: Albring et al.
counterevidence.finding: Verbal expectation alone did not cause the study's immunosuppressive response; this contradicts claims that conscious belief or explanation is universally unnecessary or sufficient.

counterevidence.author: Carvalho et al.
counterevidence.finding: The back-pain comparison was against usual care, not an attention- and ritual-matched control; the outcomes were self-report measures, not disease modification or objective structural recovery.

counterevidence.author: Lutz et al.
counterevidence.finding: No reviewed digital sham was validated as a placebo comparator, so a phone ritual cannot presently be represented as a proven substitute for a pill ritual.

open_questions.question: What are the exact active and inactive ingredients, dosage form, shipping practices, and product terms for Copables' gummies?
Which components of a Copables protocol are the pill, written card, cognitive restructuring, explanatory rationale, reminders, and human support, if any?
Is there a trial directly comparing physical open-label placebo, a digital ritual matched for contact/time, and no-treatment or usual-care controls for the same condition?
Have the Carvalho 2016 back-pain effects been independently replicated with larger samples, blinded assessment, and durable objective functional outcomes?

sources_to_verify.author: Copables Ltd.
sources_to_verify.finding: Marketing page supports the existence of protocols and depicted gummies, not verified pill composition or clinical efficacy.

sources_to_verify.author: Copables Ltd.
sources_to_verify.finding: Company science page makes detailed efficacy and mechanism assertions; each linked primary study and each product-specific extrapolation should be checked independently.
